subject: Emotions
title: Disgust and Nausea
description: A quick win: understand Disgust and Nausea.

hook.text: Your brain can make you vomit from a thought alone. No toxin required—just a vivid enough idea.

buildup.text: Nausea is disgust's enforcement arm. The brain triggers it to physically eject or avoid a threat.

discovery.text: Motion sickness exploits this system. Conflicting signals convince your brain you've been poisoned.

twist.text: Pregnant women get extra nausea in the first trimester to protect the vulnerable embryo from toxins.

climax.text: Nausea is so powerful because false alarms are cheap. Vomiting wastes a meal; food poisoning can kill.

punchline.text: Your body would rather waste food than risk poison.

quiz.question: Why does morning sickness occur in the first trimester?
